# Compatibility matrix

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/generate-compatibility-matrix.mjs` from deploy/native/support-matrix.json, deploy/native/interception-matrix.json and docs/evidence/real-host/*.json. Do not edit by hand: scripts/compatibility-matrix.test.mjs fails when this file is stale. -->

Which host versions and platforms each Singularity AIDR agent connector has actually been
tested on, which interception points it enforces, and what the host does when the AIDR hook
cannot answer. Anything not listed as tested here is untested, not supported-by-default.

Release decision recorded in the support matrix (reviewed 2026-09-30): **NO-GO**.

## Tested host versions

A connector is listed as tested only where a real-host acceptance record exists: the real,
unmodified host binary ran with AIDR installed and a scripted mock model supplied the tool
calls. That proves the host honours AIDR at its interception points for those calls on that
host version and platform; it does not prove behaviour with a real model, on other host
versions or on other platforms.

| Connector | Status | Tested host version | Tested on | AIDR artefact | Runtime requirement | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Tested on one host version | 2.1.296 (Claude Code) (pinned 2.1.282) | linux/x64, 2026-10-11 | development build | Node.js >=22.12.0 | [guide](platform-guides/claude-code.md) |
| Cursor | **Preview — no real-host acceptance evidence yet** | none | none | `aidr-cursor` 0.6.0 | extension engine `vscode ^1.97.0` | [guide](platform-guides/cursor.md) |
| VS Code | **Preview — no real-host acceptance evidence yet** | none | none | `aidr-cursor` 0.6.0 | extension engine `vscode ^1.97.0` | [guide](platform-guides/cursor.md) |
| OpenClaw | Tested on one host version | OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac) | linux/x64, 2026-10-11 | development build | Node.js >=22.12.0 | [guide](platform-guides/openclaw.md) |
| OpenCode | Tested on one host version | 1.18.32 | linux/x64, 2026-10-11 | development build | Node.js >=22.12.0 | [guide](platform-guides/opencode.md) |
| Codex CLI | Tested on one host version | codex-cli 0.141.0 | linux/x64, 2026-10-11 | development build | Node.js >=22.12.0 | [guide](platform-guides/codex.md) |

Host vendors change hook schemas and tool-call formats between releases. Treat every host
version not listed above as unverified and repeat the acceptance run (`pnpm test:e2e:real-host`)
before rolling out a host upgrade.

## Host failure behaviour

Every connector answers its own internal errors with a deny (or block): it fails closed.
That guarantee ends where the host stops asking. When the host never runs the hook (disabled,
removed or untrusted) or kills it before it answers (crash, host timeout), no verdict exists
and the host decides; the rows below record what each host does.

| Connector | Hook or plugin disabled / not trusted | Hook process killed or crashed | Offline | Large or binary tool output | Connector internal error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Call runs (host fails open) | Call runs (host fails open) | See notes below | See notes below | Call blocked (observed on the real host) |
| Cursor | Call runs (host fails open) | Not observed on a real host | See notes below | See notes below | Deny returned by the connector; not observed on a real host |
| VS Code | Call runs (host fails open) | Not observed on a real host | See notes below | See notes below | Deny returned by the connector; not observed on a real host |
| OpenClaw | Call runs (host fails open) | Not observed on a real host | See notes below | See notes below | Call blocked (observed on the real host) |
| OpenCode | Call runs (host fails open) | Not observed on a real host | See notes below | See notes below | Call blocked (observed on the real host) |
| Codex CLI | Call runs (host fails open) | Call runs (host fails open) | See notes below | See notes below | Call blocked (observed on the real host) |

Notes per connector:

- **Claude Code**: host-mediated hook; in-process errors emit an explicit deny, but a disabled hook is fail-open and a hook process killed before it writes a verdict is fail-open (observed on Claude Code 2.1.282).
  - Hook or plugin disabled / not trusted: A disabled or unregistered plugin means the host never starts the PreToolUse process, so no verdict is produced and the tool call proceeds.
  - Hook process killed or crashed: Observed on Claude Code 2.1.282 (linux/x64): a PreToolUse hook process SIGKILLed before it writes a verdict is treated as a non-blocking hook error and the tool call runs. In-process errors are converted into an explicit deny; the connector's inspection deadline and integrity-failure paths were observed to block on the same host.
  - Offline: Detection is local by default and needs no network; the network-dependent reputation legs report themselves unavailable and are never treated as clean.
  - Large or binary tool output: Large output is marked incomplete and replaced, and input above the parse ceiling, a missed deadline or an internal error is answered with a quarantine replacement chosen by tool name (MCP text block, Bash required fields). Claude PostToolUse still runs after the tool, other built-in result shapes that cannot be parsed or are unknown cannot be replaced (the host rejects a guessed shape and keeps the original), and no real-host same-turn acceptance exists for large or MCP results.
- **Cursor**: handled hook failures return deny and managed entries request failClosed: true; real-host enforcement of timeout or process termination remains unverified.
  - Hook or plugin disabled / not trusted: A disabled extension means the host never runs the hook, so no verdict is produced and the tool call proceeds.
  - Hook process killed or crashed: The entry point answers any in-process error with a deny response, but a hook process killed before it writes that response is not covered by the guarantee and has not been observed on a real host.
  - Offline: Detection is local by default and needs no network; the network-dependent reputation legs report themselves unavailable and are never treated as clean.
  - Large or binary tool output: Output above the 256 KiB ceiling is returned as coverage_limited and never classified clean, but Cursor exposes no output replacement for non-MCP tools, so the warning is advisory only.
- **VS Code**: handled hook failures return deny; real-host enforcement of timeout or process termination remains unverified.
  - Hook or plugin disabled / not trusted: A disabled extension means the host never runs the hook, so no verdict is produced and the tool call proceeds.
  - Hook process killed or crashed: The entry point answers any in-process error with a deny response, but a hook process killed before it writes that response is not covered by the guarantee and has not been observed on a real host.
  - Offline: Detection is local by default and needs no network; the network-dependent reputation legs report themselves unavailable and are never treated as clean.
  - Large or binary tool output: Output above the ceiling is marked coverage_limited, but VS Code PostToolUse is after execution and its response cannot replace bytes already returned to the model. The current block response does not establish output containment.
- **OpenClaw**: in-process plugin callback; a removed plugin means no interception at all.
  - Hook or plugin disabled / not trusted: A removed or unloaded plugin registers no callback, so the gateway enforces nothing for the tool call.
  - Hook process killed or crashed: The callback catches its own evaluation errors and blocks, but a callback that is killed by the gateway process has not been observed on a real host.
  - Offline: Detection is local by default and needs no network; the network-dependent reputation legs report themselves unavailable and are never treated as clean.
  - Large or binary tool output: Opaque binary output is not decoded or inspected; it is marked incomplete, so the pre-model tool-result middleware quarantines it on the embedded runner (unit-tested, not host-accepted with a binary result), the transcript copy is replaced and a correlated outbound response is withheld.
- **OpenCode**: in-process plugin; a removed plugin means no interception at all.
  - Hook or plugin disabled / not trusted: A removed plugin registers no hook, so the CLI enforces nothing for the tool call.
  - Hook process killed or crashed: The hook catches its own evaluation errors and denies, but a hook killed before it throws has not been observed on a real host.
  - Offline: Detection is local by default and needs no network; the network-dependent reputation legs report themselves unavailable and are never treated as clean.
  - Large or binary tool output: Oversized or opaque output is not classified clean and replacement is attempted, but unsupported or immutable result shapes can leave the original visible. OpenCode's acceptance of the mutation before same-turn model consumption is unverified.
- **Codex CLI**: native PreToolUse and UserPromptSubmit hooks; the host fails open on a crashing or untrusted hook, so the connector maps ask to an explicit deny and answers its own internal errors with a deny or block.
  - Hook or plugin disabled / not trusted: An untrusted or unregistered hook is not run at all, so the tool call proceeds without a verdict.
  - Hook process killed or crashed: The declared connector contract records a fail-open host failure boundary for a hook process that crashes, times out or emits malformed output.
  - Offline: Detection is local by default and needs no network; the network-dependent reputation legs report themselves unavailable and are never treated as clean.
  - Large or binary tool output: The connector has no output-side hook at all, so no tool response is inspected and none is reported as clean.

## Known bypasses and unobserved behaviour

### Claude Code

Known bypasses:

- Running the model against a file or shell channel the harness does not route through PreToolUse
- Direct network access that never constructs a tool call
- A UserPromptSubmit hook process killed before it answers cannot block the prompt (host behaviour); only the prompt text is inspected

Not observed on a real host:

- Same-turn blocking with a real (non-scripted) model; the real-host record uses a scripted mock model
- Behaviour when the host vendor ships a new hook schema

### Cursor

Known bypasses:

- Extension disabled by the operator
- Tools executed outside the extension host (an external terminal)

Not observed on a real host:

- Headless agent enforcement coverage on a real Cursor host
- A new Cursor version that changes the tool API
- Real-host confirmation that failClosed and explicit-deny responses are enforced for preToolUse/MCP events

### VS Code

Known bypasses:

- Extension disabled by the operator
- Tools executed outside the extension host (an external terminal)

Not observed on a real host:

- Enforcement coverage across the currently shipped VS Code minor versions
- VS Code Local activation with chat.useClaudeHooks enabled and native editFiles interception

### OpenClaw

Known bypasses:

- Plugin removed or the gateway started without it
- Pre-model tool-output quarantine needs plugins.entries.aidr-openclaw.enabled: true and the embedded runner; the Codex harness relay and after_tool_call alone do not keep a tool result from the same-turn model
- The before_agent_run prompt gate runs only in the embedded and CLI runners (not the Codex or Copilot harnesses), and a non-bundled plugin needs plugins.entries.aidr-openclaw.hooks.allowConversationAccess: true

Not observed on a real host:

- Same-turn model blocking through a running gateway (only the embedded `agent --local` runner is recorded)
- Gateway version matrix

### OpenCode

Known bypasses:

- Plugin removed or the CLI invoked with the plugin path overridden
- Provider streams that bypass the plugin's tool boundary
- chat.message prompt protection inspects the user's own text parts only; synthetic parts OpenCode generates (such as attached file contents) are not inspected

Not observed on a real host:

- Cases that require a live model provider credential (the real-host record uses a scripted mock model)
- Interactive TUI presentation of a blocked prompt

### Codex CLI

Known bypasses:

- Host fails open when hook execution is unavailable
- No output-side (pre-model) interception is claimed for this host: the PostToolUse handler inspects Bash and MCP results after execution, and the 0.141.0 host source replaces a blocked result with the reason, but no real-host run has observed that replacement
- The packaged PreToolUse matcher ^(Bash\|apply_patch\|mcp__.+)$ covers Bash, apply_patch and MCP (mcp__*) tools; MCP coverage follows the 0.141.0 host source and has no real-host record, and other local function tools (for example update_plan) do not invoke the AIDR hook
- Hosted and specialized tool paths may bypass the host tool-hook path
- Prompt protection needs the UserPromptSubmit handler registered and trusted separately; an untrusted, crashed or timed-out prompt hook lets the prompt through, and codex exec shows no reason text for a blocked prompt

Not observed on a real host:

- Verification against a Codex release newer than 0.141.0
- Host-level tamper resistance (for example a patched host binary)

## Evidence limitations

Every acceptance record states its own limits:

- The model is a scripted loopback mock: this proves the host honours AIDR at its interception boundary for the scripted call, not how a real model behaves or how broad detection is.
- The AIDR artefact is the development build from this checkout (`pnpm build`), not a signed commercial release; signed-manifest verification is exercised only as the induced internal-error case.
- Exercised on linux/x64 only; other sold platforms and architectures are not covered by this record.
- Each scenario is one non-interactive turn; interactive approval dialogs and long sessions are not exercised.

See also [upgrade notes](upgrade-notes.md) and the [support matrix README](../deploy/native/README.md).
